title: Grade 4 CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION — 2.5 Joseph interprets a Dream

pages.lesson:
PAGE 1: Overview

OVERVIEW
========

In Genesis 41:14-24 and 28-30, Pharaoh tells Joseph two dreams and Joseph says that only God can give the meaning. In this sub-strand you will retell that account, learn to depend on God's wisdom, and recite Proverbs 1:7 about the fear of the LORD.

## Strand 2.0: The Holy Bible
Sub-strand 2.5: Joseph interprets a Dream
Suggested lessons: 3

## Learning outcomes
By the end of the sub-strand, the learner should be able to:
a) retell the story of Joseph interpreting a dream
b) apply lessons learnt by depending on God’s wisdom
c) recognise that, ‘the fear of God is the beginning of wisdom.’

## Key inquiry questions
1. How was Joseph able to interpret dreams?

## Core competencies
• Learning to learn: the skill of sharing experiences is nurtured as learners share dreams they have dreamt about.

## Values
• Love: is inculcated as they learn how Joseph loved God and his adopted country Egypt by ensuring they had food security.

## Pertinent and contemporary issues
• Leadership: is nurtured as they learn how Joseph exhibited good governance.

## Links to other learning areas
• English: speaking skills are applied as learners share different experiences.
• Creative Arts: creative skills are enhanced as learners draw, dramatise and sing songs.

## Source
• KICD Grade 4 Christian Religious Education Curriculum Design (Revised 2024) — Strand 2.0 The Holy Bible, Sub-strand 2.5 Joseph interprets a Dream
• Genesis 41:14-24, 28-30; Proverbs 1:7

PAGE 2: Lesson 1: Pharaoh's dreams and Joseph's answer

LESSON 1: PHARAOH'S DREAMS AND JOSEPH'S ANSWER
==============================================

## What you will learn
• Retell Genesis 41:14-24 and 28-30.
• State what the dreams meant according to verses 28-30.

Curriculum outcomes: a) retell the story of Joseph interpreting a dream

## Introduction
Pharaoh, the king of Egypt, had dreams that troubled him. None of his magicians could explain them. He sent for Joseph, who was brought from the prison.

## Notes
Read Genesis 41:14-24 and 28-30 in turns. Stay inside those verses when you retell the story.

### Joseph is brought to Pharaoh
Pharaoh sent for Joseph. Joseph was brought quickly from the dungeon. He shaved, changed his clothes, and came in. Pharaoh said he had dreamed a dream and no one could interpret it. He had heard that Joseph could interpret a dream when he heard it.

Joseph answered, "I cannot do it, but God will give Pharaoh the answer he desires."

### The two dreams
Pharaoh said he stood on the bank of the Nile. Seven fat, healthy cows came up and grazed. Then seven thin, ugly cows came up and ate the seven fat cows, but they still looked thin. He woke up.

He slept again and saw seven full, good heads of grain growing on one stalk. Then seven thin heads, scorched by the east wind, sprouted and swallowed the seven good heads. He told the magicians, and none of them could explain it.

### The meaning in verses 28-30
Joseph said that God had shown Pharaoh what He was about to do. Seven years of great plenty were coming in Egypt. After them would come seven years of famine. The famine would be so severe that the years of plenty would be forgotten, and the famine would ruin the land.

The passage you are reading does not include later advice about storing grain. Do not add it. What these verses teach is clear: God showed the seven good years and the seven years of famine, and Joseph would not take the credit.

Draw Joseph standing before Pharaoh and colour the picture. Dramatise the moment Joseph says that he himself cannot interpret the dream.

## Key words
• interpret — to explain the meaning
• famine — a long, severe lack of food
• Pharaoh — the title of the king of Egypt
• dungeon — the prison from which Joseph was brought

## Activity: Read and dramatise the dreams
You will need: Bible, Paper, Colours
1. Read Genesis 41:14-24 and 28-30 in turns.
2. Dramatise Joseph before Pharaoh, including Joseph's words that he cannot interpret the dream but God will give the answer.
3. Draw and colour Joseph standing before Pharaoh.
4. Retell the two dreams and their meaning without adding events from other verses.

## Practice
1. Where was Joseph brought from, and what did he do before he saw Pharaoh?
2. What did Joseph say when Pharaoh asked him to interpret the dream?
3. What did the dreams mean in Genesis 41:28-30?

## Summary
• Pharaoh dreamed of seven fat cows and seven thin cows, and of seven good heads of grain and seven thin ones.
• Joseph said he could not interpret the dream, but God would.
• The meaning was seven years of plenty followed by seven years of famine.

### Answers to practice
1. He was brought from the dungeon. He shaved and changed his clothes.
2. He said he could not do it, but God would give Pharaoh the answer.
3. Seven years of great plenty would come in Egypt, followed by seven years of famine.

PAGE 3: Lesson 2: Depending on God's wisdom

LESSON 2: DEPENDING ON GOD'S WISDOM
===================================

## What you will learn
• Explain how Joseph depended on God's wisdom.
• Apply that lesson when he or she does not know an answer.

Curriculum outcomes: b) apply lessons learnt by depending on God’s wisdom

## Introduction
Joseph was given a hard question by a king. His first words were that he could not answer it by himself. That is what depending on God's wisdom looks like.

## Notes
Wisdom is knowing the right meaning and the right thing to do. Joseph did not pretend. Genesis 41:16 says, "I cannot do it." Then he pointed Pharaoh to God. The answer about plenty and famine was God's answer, given through Joseph.

### Lessons from the story
- Do not boast. Joseph refused to claim a power he did not have.
- Ask God for wisdom before you speak about things too big for you.
- God knows the future. The seven years were His plan made known to Pharaoh.
- Use God's gift to help people. The meaning of the dream warned Egypt about famine so the country could face it. Joseph loved God, and the warning was for the good of the land where he lived.
- A leader tells the truth even to a powerful person. Joseph told the king both the good years and the hard years.

### Depending on God in Grade 4
You are not asked to interpret a king's dream. You are asked to depend on God in smaller ways:

- Pray before a test, then study. Do not cheat.
- When friends ask you to decide something confusing, pray and ask a parent or teacher.
- If you do not know, say "I do not know" instead of inventing an answer. Joseph said he could not do it.
- Thank God when you understand a lesson.
- Use what you know to help the class, not to show off.

Share a dream you have had only as a personal story. Do not claim you know its secret meaning. The Bible's point is that God gave Pharaoh the meaning, not that every dream we have must be explained by us. Mention three lessons from Joseph and choose one to practise this week.

## Key words
• wisdom — knowing what is true and what is right to do
• depend — to rely on someone instead of trusting only yourself

## Activity: Three lessons from Joseph
You will need: Bible, Exercise book
1. Mention three lessons learnt from Genesis 41:14-24 and 28-30.
2. In pairs, share a dream you have dreamt, without claiming a hidden meaning.
3. Say one way you will depend on God's wisdom this week.
4. Sing a song related to the story.

## Practice
1. How was Joseph able to interpret Pharaoh's dream?
2. State two lessons from the story.
3. What should you do when you do not know an answer?

## Summary
• Joseph depended on God and refused to take the credit.
• God showed that seven plentiful years would be followed by famine.
• We depend on God's wisdom by praying, telling the truth, and not pretending.

### Answers to practice
1. He could not do it by himself. God gave Pharaoh the answer.
2. Any two: do not boast; ask God for wisdom; God knows what is coming; use God's gift to help people; tell the truth to those in authority.
3. Say that you do not know, pray, and ask God for wisdom instead of inventing an answer.

PAGE 4: Lesson 3: The fear of the LORD

LESSON 3: THE FEAR OF THE LORD
==============================

## What you will learn
• Recite Proverbs 1:7.
• Explain that the fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge and wisdom.

Curriculum outcomes: c) recognise that, ‘the fear of God is the beginning of wisdom.’

## Introduction
Joseph feared God more than he feared looking weak before Pharaoh. Proverbs 1:7 says that this kind of fear is where knowledge begins.

## Notes
Proverbs 1:7 says, "The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge, but fools despise wisdom and instruction."

### What the fear of the LORD means
This fear is not the terror that makes you run from a cruel person. It is deep respect for God. You take Him seriously. You hate what He hates. You listen when He speaks. The learning outcome calls this the beginning of wisdom. The verse itself says the beginning of knowledge. Knowledge and wisdom belong together here: you start to know what is true, and you start to live wisely, when you reverence God.

A fool, in this verse, is not a person who cannot do sums. A fool is a person who looks down on wisdom and will not be taught. Joseph did the opposite. He let God teach him the meaning of the dream.

### How this fits Joseph
Joseph said, "I cannot do it," because he knew the interpretation belonged to God. That is the fear of the LORD. He did not despise God's instruction. He passed it on to Pharaoh, including the hard news about famine.

### Living it
- Recite Proverbs 1:7 every morning this week.
- Obey a correction from a parent or teacher. That is refusing to despise instruction.
- Pray before you make a choice.
- Do not laugh at someone who is trying to learn.
- Remember that wisdom starts with God, not with showing off.

When you fear the LORD, you can stand before a hard question the way Joseph stood before Pharaoh: humble, truthful, and sure that God gives wisdom.

## Key words
• fear of the LORD — deep respect for God that takes Him seriously
• knowledge — knowing what is true
• instruction — teaching that shows you what to do

## Activity: Recite Proverbs 1:7
You will need: Bible, Flash cards
1. Read Proverbs 1:7 and write it on a flash card.
2. Recite it until you can say it without looking.
3. Explain in your own words what the fear of the LORD means.
4. Say how Joseph showed this fear before Pharaoh.
5. Sing a song thanking God for wisdom.

## Practice
1. Recite Proverbs 1:7.
2. What does the fear of the LORD mean in this verse?
3. How did Joseph show that he feared God?

## Summary
• Proverbs 1:7: the fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge.
• This fear is deep respect, not panic.
• Joseph showed it by giving God the credit for the interpretation.

### Answers to practice
1. The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge, but fools despise wisdom and instruction.
2. Deep respect for God, taking Him seriously and listening to His instruction.
3. He refused to claim the interpretation for himself and said God would give the answer.
pages.quiz:
REVISION QUIZ — 2.5 JOSEPH INTERPRETS A DREAM
========================================

Answer all the questions, then mark yourself on the Answers tab.

1. Which passage tells of Joseph before Pharaoh in this sub-strand?
   A. Genesis 41:14-24, 28-30
   B. Judges 14:5-9
   C. Luke 19:2-10
   D. Numbers 22:1-6

2. Joseph was brought from...
   A. the palace kitchen
   B. the dungeon
   C. Canaan that same morning
   D. the temple

3. In the first dream, the thin cows...
   A. ate the seven fat cows
   B. turned into grain
   C. left Egypt
   D. spoke to Pharaoh

4. What did Joseph say he could not do?

5. The dreams meant...
   A. seven days of rain
   B. seven years of plenty and then seven years of famine
   C. seven kings visiting Egypt
   D. seven donkeys on the road

6. Joseph was able to give the meaning because...
   A. he was cleverer than God
   B. God gave the answer
   C. the magicians whispered it
   D. he had read Pharaoh's diary

7. A learner who depends on God's wisdom will...
   A. pretend to know everything
   B. pray, tell the truth, and refuse to cheat
   C. ignore all teachers
   D. boast before answering

8. Proverbs 1:7 says the fear of the LORD is the beginning of...
   A. riches
   B. knowledge
   C. famine
   D. jokes

9. The fear of the LORD in Proverbs 1:7 means...

10. Fools, in Proverbs 1:7, are people who...
   A. cannot run fast
   B. despise wisdom and instruction
   C. ask God for help
   D. tell the truth to a king
pages.answers:
ANSWERS — 2.5 JOSEPH INTERPRETS A DREAM
========================================

1. A. Genesis 41:14-24, 28-30
   Those are the verses the class reads.

2. B. the dungeon
   Genesis 41:14 says he was brought from the dungeon.

3. A. ate the seven fat cows
   Pharaoh said the thin, ugly cows ate the fat cows.

4. He could not interpret the dream by himself.
   Genesis 41:16 says, "I cannot do it," and points Pharaoh to God.

5. B. seven years of plenty and then seven years of famine
   Genesis 41:29-30 states the seven years of abundance and the seven years of famine.

6. B. God gave the answer
   Joseph said God would give Pharaoh the answer he desired.

7. B. pray, tell the truth, and refuse to cheat
   Depending on God includes honesty and prayer, as Joseph refused to take the credit.

8. B. knowledge
   The verse says the fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge.

9. Deep respect for God that listens to wisdom and instruction.
   It is not hatred of God, and it is not the same as panicking.

10. B. despise wisdom and instruction
   The verse says fools despise wisdom and instruction.
